name: Wild Adventures Theme Park
unique: A theme park grown out of a small petting zoo into a full coaster park with a water park and a zoo attached, on the edge of a town of 55,000, which should not be able to support it and does.
buzz: The wooden coaster and the animals in the same day is the appeal for families. Buy tickets online, the gate price is steep.

name: Grand Bay Wildlife Management Area
unique: Eight thousand acres of blackwater swamp, cypress and sandhill where the boardwalk climbs a fire tower over the bay and alligators sun on the banks below.
buzz: The tower view across the cypress is the surprise so close to the interstate. Early morning is the only time for birds.

name: The Crescent
customer: House tourists, garden people, wedding parties
unique: An 1898 Queen Anne house with a curved colonnade, built by a turpentine and timber family, now the city garden center with camellias and old oaks around it.
buzz: The porch and the curve of the facade are the photograph. Small inside, and the grounds are the better half.

name: Annette Howell Turner Center for the Arts
unique: A downtown arts center with five galleries, working studios for pottery, glass and painting, and a schedule of classes open to visitors passing through.
buzz: Free galleries and a serious studio program. The glass and pottery classes fill early in the season.

name: Valdosta Wake Compound
unique: A cable wake park on a lake south of town, pulling riders around a course of kickers and rails without a boat, with a beginner cable and rental gear.
buzz: The beginner cable makes it usable on day one and the advanced line is legit. Summer evenings book out.

name: South Georgia Kartway
unique: A dirt kart track running weekly classes where kids and adults race the same night, with a grandstand close enough to smell the fuel.
buzz: Cheap, loud and genuinely competitive, with families racing out of trailers. The kids' classes are the best racing.

name: Lowndes County Historical Museum
unique: A county museum in a 1913 Carnegie library with the turpentine, tobacco and railroad history of Valdosta, plus a room on the man who gave the town its name and never visited.
buzz: Volunteer run with real depth on the piney woods economy. The Carnegie building is half the reason to go.

name: Copeland African American Museum
unique: A university collection of African and African American art and artifacts on the Valdosta State campus, assembled by a local family and opened to the public.
buzz: Small, free and thoughtfully shown. It is on a college campus, so check term hours.

name: Azalea City Trail
unique: A paved greenway threading Valdosta's parks and neighborhoods, passing the azalea plantings that gave the town its name, with the whole thing rideable in an afternoon.
buzz: In March the azaleas make it worth a detour. The rest of the year it is a good flat bike ride with shade.

name: A-Maze-N-Cane
unique: A maze cut into nine acres of standing sugar cane rather than corn, with walls tall enough to actually get lost in and a cane grinding and syrup boil at the end.
buzz: Cane is taller and denser than corn and the difference is obvious once you are in it. The syrup boiling is the part adults like.

name: Berrien County Courthouse
unique: An 1898 courthouse still in daily use at the centre of a town named for Nashville, Tennessee, with the original brick and a square that has kept its shape.
buzz: One of the older working courthouses in south Georgia. Five minutes, and the square around it is pleasant.

name: Southern Grace Farms
unique: A Berrien County farm with u-pick fields, a market and family events through the year, the kind of place where the produce is picked the same morning it is sold.
buzz: Good strawberries and a relaxed setup without the carnival rides. Check what is in season before driving out.

name: Brooks County Courthouse
unique: A courthouse on a square in a town incorporated in 1859, in a county named for a congressman who was beaten nearly to death in the House chamber over slavery.
buzz: The Preston Brooks story is the thing to read up on before you arrive. The square is quiet and the building is handsome.

name: Betty Sheffield Memorial Camellia Garden
dates: Year round, bloom November to March
unique: A camellia collection named for a local grower whose varieties went around the world, planted in a small town park that blooms in the dead of winter.
buzz: Camellia people make the trip in January when everything else is brown. Almost nobody else knows it is here.

name: Southwind Sporting Clays
company: Southwind Sporting Clays and Quail Hunting Preserve
unique: A sporting clays course and quail preserve on south Georgia plantation land, with a station layout through the pines and guides and dogs for the bird hunts.
buzz: The course is well laid out and the quail hunting is the real plantation experience. Book ahead in season.

name: Historic Station No. 11 Train Depot
unique: A restored railroad station in a town that grew on the lumber and turpentine trade, now an event space on the old line into the Okefenokee country.
buzz: Small and well kept, with the original platform. A natural stop on the way to the swamp.

name: Bruce's Nut-N-Honey Farm
unique: A south Georgia farm selling its own honey and pecans from the property, with the hives and the shelling operation behind the shop.
buzz: Local honey and fresh pecans at farm prices. Call first in winter, hours are seasonal.

name: Clinch County Courthouse
unique: The courthouse of one of the largest counties in Georgia by area and one of the smallest by population, on the edge of the Okefenokee watershed.
buzz: A quick stop, and the county itself is the point, a place where the swamp still sets the terms.

name: Alapaha River Canoeing
unique: A blackwater river that runs through Atkinson County with sandbars, cypress and almost no development, dropping into the Suwannee system below.
buzz: No outfitter, so bring your own boat and shuttle. Water levels swing hard and the river is best after rain.

name: Minnie Corbitt House Museum
unique: A restored house in Pearson becoming the county museum, holding the photographs, farm tools and family records of Atkinson County and its two towns.
buzz: Volunteer run and by appointment. Ask about the turpentine camps that cleared this county.

name: Atkinson County Farm Country
unique: Tobacco, peanuts and blueberries on the flatwoods between the Alapaha and the Willacoochee, with farm stands at the crossroads and nobody in a hurry.
buzz: This is drive and look country rather than a destination. Blueberry season in June is when the stands are worth stopping for.

name: Echols County Courthouse
unique: A modest mid century courthouse in the least populous county in Georgia, with no incorporated towns and a population under four thousand.
buzz: People collect counties and this is one of the rarest. The building is plain and the fact of it is the interest.

name: Alapaha River at Statenville
dates: Year round, best in high water
unique: A blackwater river crossing the county with sandbars and cypress swamp, one of the few public ways into a county that is mostly pine plantation and swamp.
buzz: Quiet water with good bream fishing. The river rises and falls fast, so check the gauge before launching.

name: Echols County Pine Flatwoods
unique: County roads running straight through pine flatwoods and cypress ponds where swallow tailed kites hunt in summer and the only traffic is a logging truck.
buzz: Birders drive these roads in June for kites and Bachman's sparrows. Bring a map, cell service is thin.

name: Stuckey's and the Pecan Log Roll
customer: Road trippers, candy people, nostalgia hunters
unique: The town where W.S. Stuckey sold his first pecan log roll from a roadside stand in 1937, starting a chain of teal roofed shops that once lined every highway to Florida.
buzz: The log roll still tastes like a 1970s road trip. The story of the chain's rise and collapse is the more interesting part.

name: Mister Angel Monument
unique: The grave and monument of Mister Angel, the goat that served as the University of Georgia's first mascot before Uga, buried here in his home county.
buzz: A genuinely odd piece of college football history in a small town cemetery. Georgia fans make the detour.

name: Dodge County History and Farm Country
unique: Peanut, cotton and pecan country around Eastman with farm supply stores, a rail line through the middle and the low brick downtown that served it.
buzz: Not a stop so much as a stretch of road worth taking slowly. Pecans in autumn are the reason to pull over.

name: Hawkinsville Harness Racing
dates: Winter training season, race days in season
customer: Horse people, families, gamblers at heart
unique: A town that calls itself the Harness Capital of the World, where standardbreds train on a half mile track through the winter and race days draw a crowd to the rail.
buzz: You can watch morning workouts for nothing and stand at the rail with the trainers. It is the only place in Georgia doing this at this scale.

name: Hawkinsville Old Opera House
unique: A 1907 city auditorium with a pressed tin ceiling and a horseshoe balcony, restored and running plays, concerts and community events on the Ocmulgee.
buzz: The room is the attraction, with the original balcony and tin work. Tickets are cheap and the season is community driven.

name: Ocmulgee River at Hawkinsville
unique: A wide river with sandbars and cypress below the town, part of a two hundred mile water trail that runs from Macon to the coast.
buzz: Good flatwater paddling with sandbar camps. The current is gentle enough for beginners.

name: Banks Lake National Wildlife Refuge
unique: A shallow blackwater lake full of cypress and water lilies with a boardwalk and a paddle trail, formed when a grist mill dam backed up the creek in the last century.
buzz: The cypress and lilies in spring are the picture, and the boardwalk makes it easy. Alligators are common and unbothered.

name: Lakeland Murals
unique: More than thirty life size murals painted on the walls of a town of 2,900, each showing a piece of early Lakeland life, so the whole downtown reads as a picture book.
buzz: The scale for a town this size is the surprise. An hour on foot covers most of them.

name: Lee's Mill and Milltown History
unique: The grist mill site that gave Lakeland its first name, Milltown, where a three story mill dammed the creek and made the lake that is now a refuge.
buzz: The mill is gone and the lake remains, which is the whole story of this county. Pair it with the refuge boardwalk.
